text:
Colorado spent most of the night in control of the chances and still skated off with a shootout loss. The Avalanche out-chanced Dallas 2.64 to 1.87 in expected goals, led in shot attempts 63 to 49, and won roughly 64 percent of simulated replays, yet the Stars took the extra point. The sharpest swing came early in the third period, when Arttu Hyry scored a shorthanded backhand (a 33 percent chance, the best look of the night) to put Dallas up 2-1 on a play that had little to do with how the rest of the game was going.

The Avalanche answered the way their play suggested they would. Gabriel Landeskog tipped in the first goal in the second period, and Brock Nelson tied it at 2-2 in the third on a wrist shot that was only a 5 percent chance, in a period where Colorado generated 1.27 expected goals to Dallas's 0.55. Miro Heiskanen's second-period wrister, a 7 percent look, was Dallas's other goal, and he logged 30:07 of ice time along the way. Casey DeSmith did the quiet work behind him, stopping 25 of 27 shots against an expected total that would have cost him 2.64 goals, a small but real edge.

The shootout ended it. Jason Robertson and Roope Hintz scored for Dallas, while Nazem Kadri's backhand was the only Colorado goal, and Nelson's miss in the fourth round closed the door. Only 22 shots reached DeSmith's net, since Colorado's advantage lived in attempts and chance quality rather than raw volume. The loss came a night after Colorado won in Dallas, 3-2 in regulation.
